[b]Erene Federation Emergency Meeting: January 9th, 2167.[/b]

[b]Briefing:[/b]
[i]"This emergency meeting has been called by the Federation High Council, all member states must participate in this monumental decision. The Erene Federation is experiencing its biggest crisis since the start of the Marisalbic War, one which threatens the continuation of our great alliance. It has come to the attention of the High Council that multiple colonies have openly rebelled against the Federation and are threatening military action against Erene.

On the 7th of January, Zytan Hoffmann, the elected representative of the Korrin Local Authority, proclaimed independence from the Federation as the Jovian Republic of Korrin and placed himself as its first Chancellor, arresting all elements of the Federation on the moon before we could react. This was followed by the illegal independence of Ilynis and then Zeonia, which have cut all communications with the Federation and failed to deliver upon their resource obligations.

Military sources warn that an attack from beyond the Belt of Tears is likely imminent, and more colonies may choose to declare independence."
[/i]
[b]Message from the High Council:[/b]
[i]"The Federation High Council advises an immediate mobilisation and operation to pacify and reclaim the rouge colonies. These colonies are abundant in resources, and the Federation has lost significant access to materials important for our survival. Should the Federation allow these traitors to rule, they may launch an attack on Erene to secure our food sources, and our capacity to grow will be severely limited. These colonies also contain valuable technology which, should they develop them further, may seal the fate of the Federation for good. As such, the High Council calls for an attack against the breakaways. However, the decision is up to the member states. Together as One."[/i]

[b]The Consantinus Matter[/b]

It arrived via holo-disc, a summons to the capital of Lyssone from the triumvirate, vaguely worded, and painfully short. Alexander Consantinus IV did not like short messages, especially from the executive offices, either it meant the secretary was drunk again or the triumvirate was hiding news from him.

Of course news was hard to hide from Alexander, who could easily call upon the SCSID to look into the matter. However, it was clear that whatever the triumvirate wished to communicate was well hidden, as the few contacts he had made communication with following the arrival of the holo-disc had given him no answers.

Thus he embarked on the two hour trip south to the capital, a large and bustling metropolis built on the shores of the White Sea, a proper sea since the deluge of 2000 had widened it tragically, nevertheless the city had been built rapidly following the formal establishment of the first triumvirate, becoming a dense mass of grand structures lining wide boulevards with orderly parks and public spaces in between. It was both an urban planner's delight and nightmare. However, it was home to most of the functions of the Rosenmarkke government, save those too critical to leave out in the open space of the capital region. 

Arriving at the Central Office, a towering white stone structure built in the linear deco style, Alexander was ushered into an empty boardroom on the fifteenth floor, a plainly decorated affair with a large marble topped conference table with slots for holographic projections to be displayed. 

Alexander sat down in one of the seats, his white military suit and pants immaculate in their form and their appearance, and he waited.

After thirty agonising minutes the door to the room opened and in stepped in the two members of the triumvirate, General Adams, and President Angthaar. 

Greetings, began Alexander, rising to greet the two heads of state.

They nodded politely and motioned for him to sit as they sat themselves down.

Now I am sure you know why you are here, began Adams gruffly.

No, I am afraid I am not, replied Alexander.

Tsk, Gjrtrelhm mustve been drunk again. replied Angthaar with a tone of disapproval and a glance at Adams, Gjrtrelhm was the personal secretary of the general.

Never mind that, stated Adams with a dismissive wave of his hand, You are here because you have been selected to be the next chief consul, he stated as a sudden silence fell over the room.

Alexander frowned, he hadnt expected it to be so soon, the SCSID had informed him that he was a contender, but they had assured him they would stall any votes, how had the stalling failed?

W-well, I am honoured, began Alexander with feigned trepidation and honest shock, Does the committee approve? he continued, inclining his head in mild disbelief at Angthaar.

Yes Mr. Consantinus, they approved the motion earlier this morning, I do apologise for the rush of course, the death of your cousin was a deep blow and well you were the best next candidate, replied Angthaar.

To be frank Mr. Consantinus, the decision was driven by the recent declaration by Korrin to be in open rebellion to the Erene Federation, it is a major unstabilising move to the federation, and could perhaps provide a window for us to break off as well, stated Adams.

Wait, wait, hold on, Korrin is in rebellion to the Federation? enquired Alexander, leaning forward, Why was the SCSID not aware of this, why was I not informed? 

The situation has been rapidly developing sir, it is hard to get all the details, but, I do believe that we must act quickly to secure our own interests before potentially introducing our own vote in the Great Assembly to break away from the Erene Federation, replied Adams.

So I am to be consul, and I am to see the collapse of the first post-deluge state, stated Alexander half to himself.

Yes sir, replied Adams, However, if we are able to ensure that any of these spacenoid states that might follow Korrins track in declaring open rebellion are kept pacified with lucrative deals, while also ensuring the EF loses its grip on resources on Erene, then Rosenmarkke might be secure in its interests, 

Alexander huffed as he leaned back in the chair, Very well then, what do we need to do? 

Before we begin anything you need to accept the consulship sir, replied Angthaar.

Alright, I accept, though I want full assurances from the committee that they truly back me as consul, replied Alexander.

Very good sir, very good, and congratulations to you replied Adams, rising to salute the new High Consul.
---------------

[b]Lying with an Honest Face[/b]

As a corporate entity, the League did not officially exist as a state within the Federation High Council. Instead, its seat was occupied by the so-called "Vespurian Empire" of old, though many within the Ardagan System already knew that this was just a simple cover for the League's extensive politicking. Even so, in full compliance to the will of the Federation, the League sent its one representative, His Imperial Majesty Candor II Daza, to act on its behalf in Erene.

In a brief "meeting" of the Imperial Privy Council, in reality just a brief discussion with corporate representatives from SummitONE Solutions and El Howayek Group, two opposing arguments swiftly emerged.

[list]"Whatever your predispositions and presumptions about the capabilities of the Federation, Mr. FitzDavid, the fact of the matter remains that the Federation has been good to us as a legal cover." argued Euphrasia El Howayek, president and CEO of the El Howayek Group, her brow furrowing into a particularly nasty glare. "I'm not particularly enthusiastic about waging war, but we can at least send our fleets to safeguard what's left of Erene from Korrin's invasion fleet."

"There is no Federation." Gale FitzDavid of SummitONE said calmly, leaning back in his seat, taking a moment to adjust his hair. "We were called to action by something pretending to be a Federation. If we want what's best for the human race, we need to scrub ourselves clean of everything to do with the old ways. We've done wonders making the regulars comply with the circular way of life, but now it's time we do the same with our foreign affairs. There's nothing left in this world to protect but the League itself."

"So you're proposing we do nothing then?"

"I'm proposing we do something, but not for the sake of the Federation. We have nothing to gain from fighting defensive battles."

"... Excuse me?..." asked Euphrasia, clearly a bit confused. So Gale wants to abandon the Federation, and yet believes that fighting on the defensive wasn't going far enough? "You're speaking in haikus. Fess up, what're you trying to get at?"

"A defensive war is just going to be a long, drawn-out, and meaningless affair in defense of something that no longer exists." Gale began, standing up and pacing the meeting room with an even tone. Euphrasia traced Gale's movements warily. "And yet, I agree that there should be a good war to enrich the League. Only the League. I propose we accept the Federation's request and begin a mass offensive of every single one of these breakaways to test the capabilities of our military might and extract whatever we can from the sinking ship."

"What the hell? Do you seriously think the League's capable of fighting beyond the Belt?!"

"Haha! I think it's funny that you'd consider the Belt something worth fussing over! The League has more than enough resources to begin the long haul!"[/list]

At that moment, Candor II, who up to this point had been largely quiet, now raised his hand to intervene in the debate before it got out of hand. It was a symbolic gesture, that the great Emperor of the Vespurian Nation had to raise his hand for permission to speak. As courtesy, both CEOs became silent and waited for his comment.

[list]"In any case..." began the Emperor "It seems that we have a consensus on aiding our Federation... it's just that we have differing sincerities and courses of action... Ms. El Howayek, I propose you send over maybe half our [i]Speedwell[/i] inventory as an expeditionary flotilla to gauge the strengths of the Korrino armed forces, whereas we can discuss Mr. FitzDavid's ideas for another time, tomorrow maybe? In the mean time, I'll provide the Federation with the good news."

"All due respect, Your Majesty, but if we're going to do good by this League, we should do it now." Gale said, interjecting.

"I have my reservations about this plan too... The Speedwells are a very antiquated design, Your Majesty." Euphrasia opined too, clearly unconvinced with Candor II's proposal. "We'll be able to hold off any recon missions, but nothing else if Korrin is serious."

"Honestly, even the Speedwells alone are a waste. They should be used in an attack, where they were meant to be!"

"Yeah, because the Exemplar Crisis showed just how excellent they were in offensives, right Mr. FitzDavid?"

"Anything's going to get murked if they were attacked from behind!"[/list]

The Emperor raised his hand again.

[list]"In that case, I'll raise the defensive assets to six Speedwells and two gunboats on the condition that I continue discussions with Mr. FitzDavid later in the day. I understand that you two have differing views on what to do with the Federation, but Ardagan is in crisis and the world is waiting. Take it from me, I think a proposal that doesn't fully satisfy either of your interests is the best way forward."[/list]

The CEOs stared at each other awkwardly for a few seconds before very, very quietly groaning in unison. When the Emperor is eager to move through with a compromise solution, that was usually the chosen solution. Not because of any deference the CEOs had to the Emperor, mind, but because they understood that he was simply doing the job he was given: to be a compromiser.

[list]"Fine." Euphrasia said, barely even trying to hide her annoyance. "But my men will be in charge of the defensive fleet. General Montagu is a SummitONE operative."

"Whatever, have it." Gale said, waving off Euphrasia's additional conditions. "General Montagu will be busy with work anyways, have fun with your fleet."[/list]

The Emperor breathed a sigh of relief and turned to a staffer to record only the last portion of their private meeting, sending for this purpose a simple message to the Federation:

- - -

[i]"The Vespurian Empire answers the call of the High Council and shall make provision for war."[/i]

[b]Hamilton Radar Station, two miles east of the city of Jasper[/b]

The Aceldixan Confederacy lay in a state of bewilderment and excitement upon witnessing the recent events at Korrin, seeing its attempt at independence as an opportunity and a chance to strengthen Aceldixan influence within the Aktus System. Whilst Aceldixan officials spoke in St. Douglass over their next move concerning the rogue planet, men working at Hamilton Radar Station spotted something odd in the stars that could potentially shift plans in a different direction. Within the station, a young private informs his commander of a strange sighting.

Sergeant! Im seeing a very large mark on the radar here sir, and it doesnt look like an asteroid.

Now hold on there just a minute there, son, its just another commercial vessel, you dont know what youre looking at. Looky here, Ill show you.

Sergeant Willis stood up from his seat and gingerly walked down towards the young man who cried asteroid. As the sergeant reached the young mans terminal, he peered into his readings and the signature left by the object. His eyebrows furled as he read and a puzzled look grew on his face. He asked the young private:

Where were you just reading this?

Over here, Sergeant.

Show me.

The private shifted his screen over to the live recording of the outer reaches of Aceldama, and saw a large object with large, bright orange radiators upon zooming in. Upon being told to examine it further, they found that it lacked any visible markings. It really had nothing for identification, apart from the fact that it was fairly large for a ship and appeared to be a Federation design. The only thing that the Aceldixans could surmise was that the ship, whether it be pirates, Federation or Korrin, was not welcome this close to Aceldama.

Sergeant Willis sent a message to the high command in St. Douglass on the matter, as well as to the provinces surrounding Jasper. In these times of rising tensions within the Ardagan System, you could never be too careful of the unknown. The radio signal for the ship was, after much difficulty, found the ships frequency, if only for a moment. A message was sent to the ship within that slim time. The message read:

From the Confederacy of Aceldix,

You are entering the jurisdiction of the Confederacy of Aceldix. We send this message with full intention to act upon each and every ounce of our words. We hope you will heed our words and follow along peacefully. Turn your ship back, or you will face severe and dire consequences for your intrusion into Aceldixan space.

The message was short, sweet and simple. The Aceldixans had no clue what to expect, as they were unsure whose ship this even was. They were not prepared for what the ship had in tail.[/spoiler]

[b]Operation Scoria[/b]

"We've been detected, clone. Looks like everything's up to you." the captain said over the radio, his voice solemn as he prepared to detach the experimental mobile suit. "Do your mission well and you will be remembered."

"As I recall, the point of this mission is to be very quickly forgotten." NSI3-4 monotonously, though even in the empty monotony you could feel the sarcasm of the response.

"Fair enough. Show no mercy, clone. Mr. FitzDavid expects good results."

A loud [i]crack[/i] is heard as the latches connecting the mobile suit's shuttle to the [i]Kipsaga[/i] were suddenly released. Silence first, then a subtle whirring of engines. The shuttle's MPD thrusters came to life, emiting a purple glow as the shuttle continued on its flight path towards Aceldama. At that exact moment, the Kartovsky particles emanating from Aceldama would effectively kill all radio contact between the two vessels, an indicator that it was time to go.
 
Having completed its mission, the [i]Kipsaga[/i] resolved to focus all attention on itself, activating its thrusters to perform a full u-turn away from the moon, as if complying with the Aceldixan demands. To further sell the illusion, the ship would fire infrared laser communication at the Aceldixan fleet, encoded with vague "apologies" and that they were now "adjusting their paths to their intended destination". However, as the [i]Kipsaga[/i] slowly veered away into the darkness of space, the small shuttle of the Frame 167 mobile suit continued to advance into Aceldama.

Being a small celestial object, Aceldama had only a sparse atmosphere, which simplified entry procedures. Typically with these things of missions, mobile suits were meant to deploy a sort of ballute system to safely enter Erene's surface without burning up. On Aceldama though, SummitONE opted for a different solution, opting to instead have Frame 167 be embedded into a civilian shuttle for a hard, hard landing.

"Approaching mission objectives..." NSI3-4 said quietly, watching as the shuttle's camera feed slowly showed the paper thin atmosphere of Aceldama coming into full view. "... bracing for impact..."

The Miosul Styx Corporation (officially, the Miosul Styx Colony, in the council) despite the Erene Federation's call to its obligations... realistically, did not have much of a military, other than it's security force in the Styx colony. A "emergency meeting" had been called between Miosul Styx's Board of Directors, with the CEO, Delling Rembran, sitting at the helm, a seemingly divided Board of Directors all seem to be focused on one single issue for that concerned the company: money.

[pre]"The Erene Federation wants us to mobilize, and start a war that could go past the belt of tears, to fight their war. A war, that will no doubt, force us to spend more than we expected this year.[/pre] Nugen declares, her mechanical, almost disconnected voice announcing this occassion more as the daily news, rather than one of the biggest crisis the Federation's faced so far.

[pre]"It's quite clear we will have to answer the Erene Federation's call for war."[/pre] Answers Kal, it was only logical, no? A smaller, weaker Federation could mean less profit for Miosul Styx, less profit, means more loss, and more loss, was bad for business,

[pre]"Despite the... monetary effect this war will have, Miosul Styx corporation still heavily relies on trade, and resources with the rest of the Erene Federation, for how would we even profit off of this war, if our main customers are being bombed-"[/pre]

[pre]"Hmph. Figures."[/pre]

Vim Jeturk interrupts, the following silence leading for all eyes in the room to lock on him, before he makes his point, 

[pre]"Why should we be obligated to the Erene Federation only? Why restrict ourselves to one customer? Why spend more money for mobilization? If they want to fight- they'll want Miosul Styx's minerals, don't they? And so would Zeonia, Ilynis, Korrin!"[/pre]

He opens his arms, this was not a war, this was profit, a business opportunity, 

[pre]"This is could be THE most profitable year for our company's history, and you think we should restrict ourselves for it?"[/pre]

[pre]"And what's stopping us from just breaking off?"[/pre]

Asks Sarrius Zenelli, unwilling to spend a dime on defending what he saw as an outdated, dying, planet. Dependent on Spacians anyways.

[pre]"The Erene Federation has done nothing but take resources for themselves, wasting away millions- if not billions of credits to keep a dying planet alive. It was only inevitable that their own colonies would rebel against them if Erene itself has little to nothing to show for itself, why bother trying to aid the Federation? We can profit more by ourselves, selling instead to the Spacians themselves!"[/pre]

[b][pre]"Enough."[/pre][/b]

The CEO, Delling Rembran finally speaks, standing up from his chair, commanding the room with his presence, gazing around the room in silence for a few seconds, before speaking,

[pre]"It's clear that the company's interests come first in this issue. And it's clear that the company itself can take many different stands on this issue."[/pre]

The CEO's eyes shift to Vim Jetturk, assessing his proposal,

[pre]"However... it would seem that the best course of action would the Mister Jetturk's proposal, to play the two sides of this conflict for the company's advantage."[/pre]

Vim Jetturk crossed his arms, a smug grin lighting up in his face as his recommendation was taken as the company's direction. Soon, the rest of the board would follow, voting in favor of this decision, much to the dismay, and anger of a Sarrius Zenelli.

After the meeting, the Miosul Styx Colony would announce it's stance on this conflict:
[b][pre]The Miosul Styx Colony will answer the Federation High Council's call to war.[/pre][/b]

All the while, behind the scenes... preparing to reach out to the "rogue" colonies, willing to make deals.
[/i]
